verdict.rationale: AWS ships an official, documented CLI (AWS CLI v2) that controls multiple services from the terminal, supports script automation, offers console-credential login, tab completion, interactive prompting and command history, and comes pre-installed in CloudShell. That fits an AI-native user automating AWS from the command line. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of CLI use, and explicit agent-oriented CLI features (e.g. machine-readable output guidance for AI agents) in the evidence.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: With just one tool to download and configure, you can control multiple AWS services from the command line and automate them through scripts.
the AWS CLI enables you to start running commands that implement functionality equivalent to that provided by the browser-based AWS Management Console from the command prompt in your terminal program
Use your existing console credentials to programmatically access AWS with the 'aws login' CLI command.
The AWS CLI v2 can prompt you with commands, parameters, resources, documentation, and more when running an 'aws' command.
